call_points.text: Management declined to give FY27 growth or margin guidance, saying it would be better placed next quarter.
FY27 capex is maintenance only, plus a few small steel lines to be commissioned early next year.
Molded Furniture revenue was ₹80 Cr; management does not expect the segment to be a revenue driver.
Cash kept for inorganic opportunities; no buyback planned.
Chinese glassware dumping continues to slow the glass plant's scale-up.
Wim Plast merger share allotment not yet completed due to technical glitches; expected in a few weeks.
Promoter stake sale news: company says there is nothing at present, referring to its exchange clarification.

corporate_actions.subject: Annual General Meeting/Dividend - Rs 1.50 Per Sh

guidance.statement: EBITDA margin 2-2.5% higher than current levels
Capex of around ₹100 Cr for FY27
Writing instruments revenue of ₹500 Cr+ in FY27
Receivable days 10-15 days lower, below 100 days

operating_notes.text: Glassware utilisation was about 60% in Q4FY26, with the category at breakeven and peak revenue seen at ₹300 Cr and 28-30% EBITDA margin.
Opalware utilisation was about 85% in Q4FY26, with expansion planned only after current capacity is exhausted.
E-commerce and quick commerce channels accounted for nearly 17% of Q4FY26 revenue, with profitability in line with other segments.
Glassware utilisation about 60% and Opalware 80-85% in Q1FY27; glass plant sales up 30-35% over Q1FY26.
Peak revenue stated at ₹250-275 Cr for the glass plant and ₹300 Cr for the steel plant with eight lines.
Online channel 16.3% of Q1FY27 sales versus 10.4% in Q1FY26; general trade 71.1%, exports 7.3%, modern trade 5.3%.

timeline.summary: On its 29 May 2026 Q4FY26 call, Cello World guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-12% and EBITDA margin 2-2.5% higher, with steel bottle lines reaching full production from July.
On its 10 August 2026 Q1FY27 call, Cello World reported revenue of ₹526.7 Cr, EBITDA margin of 22.2% and PAT of ₹73.4 Cr, and declined to give FY27 guidance.
